steps.scene: A long, straight descent. You're tempted to slip into neutral and let the car roll down to save a bit of fuel.

options.text: Nothing — it saves fuel and does no harm
You lose control — no engine braking, less steering
The car steers more precisely without drive

question.explanation: Coasting means the engine can't drive the wheels — no engine braking, and less stability through a bend.

steps.title: The engine is a brake
steps.body: Change down a gear and the engine holds the car back for you. It slows you, settles the car, and saves the brakes.

question.prompt: How do you use the engine to help control your speed?

options.text: By changing to a lower gear
Only the brakes can slow the car
By changing to a higher gear

question.explanation: A lower gear brings engine braking. You feel it the moment you change down.

a.label: Low gear, careful brakes
a.body: Gravity is held by engine braking; the brakes do short bursts and stay cool.

b.label: High gear, brakes held on
b.body: The brakes take the whole hill, get hot, and fade just when you need them.

question.prompt: You're about to go down a steep hill. How do you control your speed?

options.text: Select a high gear and use the brakes carefully
Hold the brakes on all the way down
Select a low gear and use the brakes carefully

question.explanation: A low gear gives you engine braking; the brakes then only have to do the rest, in short applications.

steps.title: Skids have a driver
steps.body: A skid is caused by braking, steering or accelerating too harshly for the grip that's there. The weather only sets the limit.

question.prompt: What's the main cause of skidding?
question.explanation: Skidding is usually driver error. Adjust your driving to the road and weather and you keep the grip you have.

steps.title: Emergency stop with ABS
steps.prompt: Order an emergency stop in a car fitted with anti-lock brakes.

items.text: A hazard appears — you decide to stop
Apply the footbrake promptly and firmly
Hold that pressure — the pedal may judder and grate
Keep it applied until the vehicle has stopped

steps.explanation: Never pump the pedal. The juddering is the ABS working — hold firm pressure until you've stopped.

steps.title: Gentle wins on ice
steps.body: On ice, keep your speed down and use the highest gear you can. Less power at the wheels means less chance of spinning them.

question.prompt: How do you avoid wheelspin on an icy road?

options.text: Drive slowly in the highest gear possible
Use a low gear and plenty of revs to get moving

question.explanation: Torque at the wheels is what breaks them loose. A high gear and a light foot keep what grip there is.

steps.scene: A cold, clear morning. The road looks merely damp, but the tyres have gone almost silent and the steering feels light.

options.text: The road is icy — be very gentle with everything
It's only damp — ice would be visible

question.explanation: On ice the tyres make almost no noise and the steering goes light. Brake, steer and accelerate gently.
